title: Watch your cashflow, "Start when?"
caption: The right moment is the first column. Right now.

worry-early.description: The test is whether a company reaches profitability on its remaining money at current expenses and growth; worrying too early is cheap and worrying too late is dangerous.[1]

default-alive-or-default-dead.title: Paul Graham, Default Alive or Default Dead?

start-when.title: Start when
start-when.keywords: arrow from Q3 back to Q1, not when the money runs low, the first column, right now
start-when.script: Look at the arrow from Q3 back to Q1. It says: start when? Not when the money runs low. By then, the revenue is already months away. The right moment is the first column. Right now.

learning-goal.title: Learning goal
learning-goal.keywords: sales before revenue is needed, revenue trails costs, how the clock runs
learning-goal.script: So here is the point of this talk. Sales must start long before revenue is needed, because revenue trails costs. Always. It is not a sign of a bad company. It is how the clock runs.

your-four-steps.title: Your four steps
your-four-steps.keywords: cashflow view, lead list, first contact, track deals, conversion rate, sales cycle
your-four-steps.script: Your four steps. One: build your cashflow view and find your zero-cash month. Two: keep a lead list, and add to it. Three: make first contact, by cold call, inbound or network. Four: track your deals, and measure your conversion rate and your sales cycle.

this-week.title: This week
this-week.keywords: pick the first step, draw the board, find the month, how early to start
this-week.script: You do not have to do all four today. Pick the first one and do it this week. Draw the board, find the month, and you will know exactly how early you have to start.
